title: Your Eyes Are a Moon
text:
Your eyes are a moon

that shimmers

on a black lagoon


Your hair the black waves

under the moonless sky


And the flight

of the owl in the

black night
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's nocturnal sequence of moon, lagoon, hair, and owl.

title: My Tender Kitten...
text:
My tender kitten

my tender kitten!


how they make

my tender kitten tremble


my caresses on her face

and her neck


And your murders

and tortures!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the abrupt collision between private tenderness and public violence.

title: Have You Heard?
text:
Have you heard

at night

the bear-horse cry


oo—oo—oo—oo


or the coyote

alone in the night

of moonlight


uuuuuuuuuuuuuú?


well that is exactly

what these verses are.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the animal cries and lets the poem define itself as that same nocturnal sound.

title: This Will Be My Revenge
text:
This will be my revenge:

That one day the book of a famous

poet reaches your hands

and you read these lines the author wrote for you

and you do not know it.
editorial_note: The translation keeps revenge as delayed recognition withheld from the beloved.

title: Others May
text:
Others may

earn a great deal of money


But I have sacrificed

that money


to write

these songs to you


or to another whom I will sing

instead of you


or to no one.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the comic narrowing from love poem to replacement beloved to nobody.
